summary: First iteration end-to-end test for Data Wrench. All 24 backend endpoints exercised via pytest (auth, chat with heat detection, sessions, voice TTS, chart edit, library upload/list/delete, vehicles CRUD, datalog analyze, memory, settings) and all critical frontend flows verified with Playwright (login, chat reply rendering, chart editor with 40-cell modification, library upload, vehicle creation, sessions drawer). Full system is functional including the GPT-5.2 personality, heat-mode trigger, chart killer feature, and RAG library upload.

minor.issue: Initial pass returned 500 'Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 1.0146 / Max budget: 1.001' from litellm via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY. Retry ~30s later succeeded. Universal-key budget appears to be very close to the cap and occasionally throws transient budget errors. Worth flagging to ops; not a code defect.

action_items: (Optional / external) Monitor EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget — transient '500 Budget exceeded' surfaced on first chat call then auto-resolved on retry. If it recurs in production, surface a friendlier 'service over quota' message in /api/chat instead of raw exception text.
(Nice-to-have) STT (/api/voice/transcribe) was not exercised end-to-end — needs a real audio file via browser mic. Backend wiring is in place but not tested in this iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 696 lines — over the 700-line guideline soft cap. Consider splitting into routers/auth.py, routers/chat.py, routers/charts.py, routers/library.py, routers/voice.py for maintainability.
Library RAG uses naive keyword scoring (acknowledged MVP design). For production, swap to embeddings + vector search.
Chat endpoint replays last 12 turns by appending them to system_message instead of using LlmChat's multi-turn API — works but bloats system prompt and may hurt instruction adherence on long sessions.
Error messages from upstream LLM/litellm are echoed verbatim to clients ('Wrench is jammed up: {e}'). Acceptable for single-user MVP, but in multi-tenant production this leaks budget/account info.
/api/chat raises HTTPException(500) on LLM failure but persists nothing; that's correct. Consider returning 503 instead of 500 for upstream provider failures.

success_rate.backend: 100% (24/24 on retry; 20/24 on first pass due to transient budget error)

seed_data_creation: Tests create then delete: TEST_ library item, TEST_ vehicle, TEST_ memory fact. Chat tests leave 1-2 transient sessions in DB (small).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 24 cases. If chat tests fail with 'Budget has been exceeded', re-run JUST TestChat — it's a transient on the universal key. STT endpoint /api/voice/transcribe is untested (no audio fixture). Frontend uses @-alias and data-testid attrs are comprehensive — see Shell.jsx nav-* ids and per-page page-level testids.
rca of the issue: The transient 500 on /api/chat was a litellm budget-exceeded response from the OpenAI provider via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY ('Current cost: 1.0146 / Max budget: 1.001'). The cost tracker on the universal key sits right at the cap and the very next attempt succeeded — likely a billing-tracking race or per-key soft cap. Mitigation: catch litellm.BadRequestError specifically in /api/chat, /api/chart/edit, /api/datalog/analyze and return HTTP 503 with message 'AI quota exceeded — try again in a moment.' rather than raw stringified exception.
